## What it is

- The **AC30** came out in **1959** from JMI (Vox), designed by Dick Denney; the **Top Boost** circuit became standard in **1963** (Wikipedia, "Vox AC30").
- Four **EL84** valves, **cathode biased**, about 30 W, a GZ34 valve rectifier, two 12" Celestion speakers ("Blue") (Wikipedia).
- Often called class A, it is in fact **class AB**, run hot, with **no negative feedback** (Wikipedia).
- Used by the Shadows, the Beatles, Brian May and the Edge (Wikipedia).

## How it makes its sound

- The **Top Boost** is the Fender Bassman tone stack **with the middle control removed** (Wikipedia). The **tone stack** (Treble, Middle, Bass) is a passive network of three capacitors and resistors: it can only cut. This page computes its curve exactly from the component values, with the formula Yeh and Smith published in 2006 (checked there against a circuit simulator); the graph under the panel shows it. Here the middle leg is a fixed 10 kΩ resistor (unverified value).
- With no negative feedback the power valves are not held in check: they break up early and smoothly, the "chime" turning into crunch (Brian May's "smooth transition into compression", Wikipedia).
- **Cut** sits in the power amp and only takes treble away: turn it up to tame the top (here a low-pass from 18 kHz down to 1.6 kHz, the site's values).
- The **Vib-Trem** channel: vibrato wobbles the pitch, tremolo the volume. (On the real amp it is another channel; here it is applied to the Top Boost sound.)

## The amp

The Vox AC30 Top Boost's control panel, drawn after photos (positions approximate, no logos). Drag a knob (or use the arrow keys), click a switch, then press a ▶ button. The guitar is this site's pickup model; **Pedals in front** puts one of the site's pedal models before the amp. Nobody has compared the sound with a real amp. The graph shows the tone controls and the cabinet (the valves' distortion is left out of it).

## Guided tour

```{=html}
<div class="amp-step" data-amp="ac30" data-set="{&quot;volume&quot;:4,&quot;treble&quot;:7,&quot;bass&quot;:4,&quot;cut&quot;:2}" data-play="chord"><p><b>Volume 4.</b> Chiming clean.</p></div>
<div class="amp-step" data-amp="ac30" data-set="{&quot;volume&quot;:8,&quot;treble&quot;:7,&quot;bass&quot;:4,&quot;cut&quot;:2}" data-play="riff"><p><b>Volume 8.</b> The valves start to compress and crunch.</p></div>
<div class="amp-step" data-amp="ac30" data-set="{&quot;volume&quot;:8,&quot;treble&quot;:7,&quot;bass&quot;:4,&quot;cut&quot;:8}" data-play="riff"><p><b>Cut 8.</b> The same, darker.</p></div>
<div class="amp-step" data-amp="ac30" data-set="{&quot;volume&quot;:5,&quot;vt&quot;:&quot;vibrato&quot;,&quot;speed&quot;:5}" data-play="chord"><p><b>Vibrato.</b> The pitch wavers.</p></div>
<div class="amp-step" data-amp="ac30" data-set="{&quot;volume&quot;:5,&quot;vt&quot;:&quot;tremolo&quot;,&quot;speed&quot;:6}" data-play="chord"><p><b>Tremolo.</b> The volume pulses.</p></div>
```
